pointers.sentence: `ProjectState.apps` is a `cached_property` whose body is one call: a `StateApps` made from `ProjectState.real_apps` and `ProjectState.models` (`django/db/migrations/state.py:ProjectState.apps`).
Forwards, the executor renders a state, if nothing has, just before the first migration it runs on it (`django/db/migrations/executor.py:MigrationExecutor._migrate_all_forwards`).
`ModelState.render` is given a registry and returns a model class (`django/db/migrations/state.py:ModelState.render`).
An abstract base is not among a model state's bases, and its methods go with it, as Named has gone from the historical Ship's resolution order (`django/db/migrations/state.py:ModelState.from_model`).

A manager the model state does hold is made again by `ModelState.construct_managers`: it says by `BaseManager.deconstruct` how it was made, and another is made the same way, by `QuerySet.as_manager` on its queryset class or by calling its class with the same arguments (`django/db/migrations/state.py:ModelState.construct_managers`).

`StateApps` is a subclass of `Apps`, the class of the main registry, made to be changed: a model can be put in another's place in it or taken out, and the whole copied (`django/db/migrations/state.py:StateApps`).

Its comment gives the reasons: the classes of the main registry refer to that registry and so cannot be used, and their relations, for want of dependencies, go wrong in a state that holds only part of the project (`django/db/migrations/state.py:StateApps.__init__`).

It then makes an `AppConfigStub`, an `AppConfig` cut down to a label and a dictionary of models, for each label of `real_apps` and of the model states, and passes them to `Apps.__init__`, which populates a registry at once when it is given configurations (`django/db/migrations/state.py:AppConfigStub`).

Last, it runs `_check_lazy_references`, the function behind the system check of the main registry, on this one, and raises `ValueError` with the messages if anything is reported: a relation that named its target by a string is still waiting for a model that was not rendered (`django/core/checks/model_checks.py:_check_lazy_references`) ([The registry and its models](../startup/registry.md)).

A pass that renders nothing means a base that will never come, and the method raises `InvalidBasesError` itself, with the model states left over and the usual cause: inheriting, in an application with no migrations, from a model of an application that has them (`django/db/migrations/state.py:StateApps.render_multiple`).

`bulk_update` sets `Apps.ready` to false for its body, so that `clear_cache` passes over the models, and on leaving restores it and calls `clear_cache` once (`django/db/migrations/state.py:StateApps.bulk_update`).

Where `Apps.register_model` warns of, or refuses, a second class under a name that is taken, `StateApps.register_model` puts the class in the place of whatever was there, makes a stub for a label the registry lacks, and then, like the main registry, runs what was waiting for the model and clears the caches (`django/db/migrations/state.py:StateApps.register_model`).
`StateApps.unregister_model` takes a model out and leaves the caches alone; the main registry has no such method (`django/db/migrations/state.py:StateApps.unregister_model`).
`StateApps.clone` makes an empty `StateApps` with a deep copy of `Apps.all_models`, stubs of its own, and the same `real_models` (`django/db/migrations/state.py:StateApps.clone`).

`ProjectState.reload_model` returns at once on a state that is not rendered; on one that is, it has `ProjectState._find_reload_model` say which models are to be made again and gives the set to `ProjectState._reload` (`django/db/migrations/state.py:ProjectState.reload_model`).

`_find_reload_model` takes the class the registry has for the model, if it has one, as it was before the change, and collects the models related to it; reads the model state, as it is after the change, for the models its relations name, and collects each of those with the models related to it; and adds the model itself (`django/db/migrations/state.py:ProjectState._find_reload_model`).

With `delay=True` the models further away are left as they are, to be made good when `ProjectState.clear_delayed_apps_cache` has the whole state rendered afresh. "Related" then means `get_related_models_tuples`: the model's direct subclasses, the class at the other end of each of its relations, forward and reverse, and for a proxy that a relation points at, the model it stands for (`django/db/migrations/state.py:_get_related_models`).

`_reload` takes each model of the set out of the registry and gives `StateApps.render_multiple` the model states it finds for them, among `StateApps.real_models` and the project state's (`django/db/migrations/state.py:ProjectState._reload`).
*The reload each method of `ProjectState` asks for (`django/db/migrations/state.py:ProjectState.alter_field`, `django/db/migrations/state.py:ProjectState.remove_model`).*
*The reload each method of `ProjectState` asks for (`django/db/migrations/state.py:ProjectState.alter_field`, `django/db/migrations/state.py:ProjectState.remove_model`).*

What a reference is, `field_references` decides: it counts every many-to-many field to the model as a reference to any of its fields (`django/db/migrations/utils.py:field_references`) ([The field operations, and those on indexes and constraints](field-operations.md)).

`RunPython.database_forwards` calls `ProjectState.clear_delayed_apps_cache` on its from-state before it calls its function with that state's registry, and the migrate command calls it on the state the executor returns before it hands that state's registry to the receivers of `post_migrate`: a function or a receiver may ask the registry for any model (`django/db/migrations/operations/special.py:RunPython.database_forwards`, `django/core/management/commands/migrate.py:Command.handle`) ([The migrate command, showmigrations and sqlmigrate](migrate.md)).

`RunPython.database_forwards` calls `ProjectState.clear_delayed_apps_cache` on its from-state before it calls its function with that state's registry, and the migrate command calls it on the state the executor returns before it hands that state's registry to the receivers of `post_migrate`: a function or a receiver may ask the registry for any model (`django/db/migrations/operations/special.py:RunPython.database_forwards`, `django/core/management/commands/migrate.py:Command.handle`) ([The migrate command, showmigrations and sqlmigrate](migrate.md)).

`clear_delayed_apps_cache` deletes the registry from the `__dict__` of a state that is delayed and rendered, and the next read renders every model afresh (`django/db/migrations/state.py:ProjectState.clear_delayed_apps_cache`).

And `RunPython.database_backwards` passes its function the from-state's registry without that call, so a function run backwards may be given a registry that a delayed reload left inconsistent (`django/db/migrations/operations/special.py:RunPython.database_backwards`) ([`RunPython`, `RunSQL` and `SeparateDatabaseAndState`](special-operations.md)).
